# `scope_get_axle_coord`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Query the connected mount for its two axle coordinates.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (strict; native handler, 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x78e20 (64-bit build); ScopeAM5::GetAxleCoords @0xef700 |

Performs a live mount query (ScopeAM5::GetAxleCoords) and returns a two-number array. Axis units and frame are unresolved. Params are not consumed. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :GDd, :GDr.

Side effects: Live query to the mount controller for the axis coordinates; no motion.

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_get_axle_coord"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Example

Request, query - Params omitted:

```json
{"id":100,"method":"scope_get_axle_coord"}
```

Reply, ok - Invented values:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_axle_coord","result":[123.4,56.7],"code":0,"id":100}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_axle_coord","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":101}
```
